title: John 4: The Woman at the Well and the Nobleman's Son
body:
Read the chapter → [John 4](/bible/john/4)

**[John 4:1-6](/bible/john/4#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/john/4#v1)</sup> When therefore the Lord knew how the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/john/4#v2)</sup> (Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples,)
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/john/4#v3)</sup> He left Judea, and departed again into Galilee.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/john/4#v4)</sup> And he must needs go through Samaria.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/john/4#v5)</sup> Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/john/4#v6)</sup> Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.

- Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples, many of whom had begun with John.
- He must needs go through Samaria, and comes to Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Joseph was the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, so this is northern kingdom ground.

**[John 4:7-9](/bible/john/4#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/john/4#v7)</sup> There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/john/4#v8)</sup> (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/john/4#v9)</sup> Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.

- How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
- The Jews in that day were Judah, Benjamin and Levi, not all twelve tribes. The Samaritans were Ephraim, and the reason for the separation is written in the prophets.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ezra 1:5](/bible/ezra/1#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ezra/1#v5)</sup> Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, with all them whose spirit God had raised, to go up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.

    The chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests, and the Levites, went up to build the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.
  - **[Isaiah 7:8-9](/bible/isaiah/7#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/isaiah/7#v8)</sup> For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/isaiah/7#v9)</sup> And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.

    Within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people; and the head of Ephraim is Samaria.
  - **[Hosea 4:17](/bible/hosea/4#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/hosea/4#v17)</sup> Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.

    Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.

**[John 4:10-15](/bible/john/4#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/john/4#v10)</sup> Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/john/4#v11)</sup> The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that living water?
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/john/4#v12)</sup> Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/john/4#v13)</sup> Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/john/4#v14)</sup> But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/john/4#v15)</sup> The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw.

- If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink, thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water. She answers about the depth of the well.
- Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well? She names Jacob as her father. Jacob is the progenitor of one nation, and this is the ground he gave to Joseph.
- Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; it shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

**[John 4:16-19](/bible/john/4#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/john/4#v16)</sup> Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/john/4#v17)</sup> The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband:
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/john/4#v18)</sup> For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/john/4#v19)</sup> The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.

- Go, call thy husband. She answers that she has none, and he tells her she has had five, and the one she has now is not her husband.
- Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Being told her own life by a man who had never met her is what turned her.

**[John 4:20-24](/bible/john/4#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/john/4#v20)</sup> Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/john/4#v21)</sup> Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/john/4#v22)</sup> Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/john/4#v23)</sup> But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/john/4#v24)</sup> God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

- The hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Jerusalem itself was to be laid level with the ground.
- Salvation is of the Jews, because Christ sprang out of Judah.
- The true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth. Without temple, sacrifice or priesthood, a scattered people worship in sincerity and in truth, which is what Joshua charged Israel with.

  Precepts:
  - **[Luke 19:41-44](/bible/luke/19#v41)**
    > <sup>[41](/bible/luke/19#v41)</sup> And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,
    >
    > <sup>[42](/bible/luke/19#v42)</sup> Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
    >
    > <sup>[43](/bible/luke/19#v43)</sup> For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
    >
    > <sup>[44](/bible/luke/19#v44)</sup> And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

    Thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and shall not leave in thee one stone upon another.
  - **[Joshua 24:14](/bible/joshua/24#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/joshua/24#v14)</sup> Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the Lord.

    Fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth.

**[John 4:25-26](/bible/john/4#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/john/4#v25)</sup> The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/john/4#v26)</sup> Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.

- I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ. Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.

**[John 4:27-30](/bible/john/4#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/john/4#v27)</sup> And upon this came his disciples, and marvelled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why talkest thou with her?
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/john/4#v28)</sup> The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men,
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/john/4#v29)</sup> Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/john/4#v30)</sup> Then they went out of the city, and came unto him.

- The disciples marvelled that he talked with the woman, because of the separation that had been commanded, yet no man said, Why talkest thou with her?
- She left her waterpot and told the men of the city, Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?

**[John 4:31-38](/bible/john/4#v31)**

> <sup>[31](/bible/john/4#v31)</sup> In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/john/4#v32)</sup> But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/john/4#v33)</sup> Therefore said the disciples one to another, Hath any man brought him ought to eat?
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/john/4#v34)</sup> Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/john/4#v35)</sup> Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/john/4#v36)</sup> And he that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal: that both he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/john/4#v37)</sup> And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/john/4#v38)</sup> I sent you to reap that whereon ye bestowed no labour: other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours.

- My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work. The disciples took it for literal food.
- Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest. One soweth, and another reapeth.

**[John 4:39-42](/bible/john/4#v39)**

> <sup>[39](/bible/john/4#v39)</sup> And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/john/4#v40)</sup> So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/john/4#v41)</sup> And many more believed because of his own word;
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/john/4#v42)</sup> And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.

- Many of the Samaritans believed on him for the saying of the woman, and many more because of his own word, and said, We know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.

**[John 4:43-54](/bible/john/4#v43)**

> <sup>[43](/bible/john/4#v43)</sup> Now after two days he departed thence, and went into Galilee.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/john/4#v44)</sup> For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honour in his own country.
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/john/4#v45)</sup> Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.
>
> <sup>[46](/bible/john/4#v46)</sup> So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.
>
> <sup>[47](/bible/john/4#v47)</sup> When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.
>
> <sup>[48](/bible/john/4#v48)</sup> Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe.
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/john/4#v49)</sup> The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/john/4#v50)</sup> Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way.
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/john/4#v51)</sup> And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told him, saying, Thy son liveth.
>
> <sup>[52](/bible/john/4#v52)</sup> Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
>
> <sup>[53](/bible/john/4#v53)</sup> So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house.
>
> <sup>[54](/bible/john/4#v54)</sup> This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judea into Galilee.

- Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. The nobleman wants him to come down before his child dies.
- Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way. He did not need to see it first.
- The servants meet him with the news, and the hour matches. The believing is what stands out here; unbelief was always the trouble with the people, and this man believed a word without a sign.
